meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law tradition) with Offshore Special Territory attributes; Gibraltar operates under its own Companies Act 2014 and English case law is persuasive authority; the Cayman Islands applies its separate Companies Act (2022 Revision), also within the English common law tradition

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Cayman Islands: Proceeds of Crime Act (2021 Revision); Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2023 Revision); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act, 2023 and Beneficial Ownership Transparency Regulations, 2023 (non-public register administered by the Registrar of Companies); Companies Act (2022 Revision); Tax Concessions Act (2021 Revision); CIMA Guidance Notes on the Prevention and Detection of Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Proliferation Financing. ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access – both the Cayman Islands and Gibraltar maintain non-public beneficial ownership registers accessible to designated competent authorities (tax authorities, financial intelligence units and the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit); no public access to the BO register; nominee arrangements are permitted in Cayman law but the registered agent must maintain and disclose full underlying UBO records to CIMA and the Registrar upon request.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorised signatories against the UN Consolidated List; UK Consolidated List (HM Treasury ONSI); Gibraltar Sanctions List under the Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2020; EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (required for EU payment rail counterparties); OFAC SDN List (mandatory for USD settlement via US correspondent banks); and World Bank/Interpol PEP databases. Screening is required at onboarding, on each transaction above USD 10,000, and continuously via automated 24-hour re-screening. Enhanced Due Diligence applies to politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates per FATF Recommendation 12, with source-of-wealth documentation mandatory. Simplified due diligence is not available because the business is non-face-to-face and operates exclusively through digital payment rails (Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Primary: Cayman Islands General Registry – Office of the Registrar of Companies (www.ciregistry.ky) for name reservation and incorporation of the Cayman Exempted Company. Ancillary: Gibraltar Companies House (www.gibraltarcompanieshouse.gi) for mandatory name screening when the Cayman entity registers as a foreign company under Part 2 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All company names must be in English using Latin (Roman) script; no transliteration from non-Latin scripts is recognised. The proposed name must be distinguishable from existing registered names on both the Cayman and Gibraltar registries, must not be misleading, and must not imply governmental, royal, charitable or financial services status absent prior consent. The Cayman Exempted Company may omit the suffix Limited/Ltd where the Registrar grants a dispensation for an exempted company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited, Ltd (mandatory suffix for limited companies unless dispensation granted)
Trust, Trustee, Trust Company (Cayman Islands Monetary Authority consent required)
Bank, Banking, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Building Society
Royal, Crown, Imperial, Government, Commonwealth, British, Her Majesty, King, Queen
Gibraltar, Cayman (territorial name consent required from the relevant Minister/Governor)
Red Cross, Red Crescent, Olympic, United Nations, University, College, Institute (ministerial consent)
Chamber of Commerce, Co-operative, Partnership (misleading if not accurate)
Gaming, Casino, Lottery, Betting (Gibraltar Gambling Division pre-approval; prohibited absent licence)
Finance, Fund, Securities, Investment, Capital (Gibraltar Financial Services Commission consent needed)
Standard, International, Global (with caution where it implies regulatory status or monopolistic advantage)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Cayman Islands: upon rejection, the applicant (through the registered agent) may file a written appeal to the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands within 21 days of the Registrar's refusal under section 11 of the Companies Act (2022 Revision); a fee is payable and the Court may order the Registrar to register the name. The agent may alternatively submit a fresh name application with a new distinctive element; name reservations may be renewed by re-application before the 90-day window expires. Gibraltar: upon refusal by the Gibraltar Registrar, the applicant may request an internal review within 14 days citing section 47 of the Companies Act 2014 (sensitive names), or invoke the company name adjudication procedure under sections 71–78 of the Companies Act 2014 where a third party claims goodwill or confusing similarity; strict statutory deadlines apply and prompt legal representation is advised.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as a substitute for the statutory registered office. A Cayman Exempted Company must maintain a physical registered office in the Cayman Islands at the office of a CIMA-licensed corporate services provider; a pure virtual mailing address does not satisfy the Companies Act (2022 Revision). If the Cayman entity also registers as a foreign company in Gibraltar, a second physical address for service in Gibraltar is mandated under sections 26 and 330 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014. The production workshop for the handmade epoxy-resin dice may remain physically outside both jurisdictions (including a home-based founder studio) without triggering a licensed commercial presence, provided the online seller complies with local consumer-protection and tax registration rules in the founder's country of residence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 18% combined probability of an announced or unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months of operation, primarily arising from the registered agent's CIMA/GFSC compliance supervisory visits. Probability rises to 25–30% if the company publishes its registered address on Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal or the company website, or if a third-party complaint triggers a regulatory site visit. The business is classified as Low_Risk_Standard for AML purposes, so intrusive inspection is not expected, but substance documentation (board minutes, corporate records, UBO register) must remain physically retrievable at the Cayman and Gibraltar registered offices at all times.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar, 169 John Mackintosh Square, Gibraltar GX11 1AA; e-filing portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Cayman Exempted Company is not automatically within the Gibraltar tax net. If it establishes a physical place of business or derives Gibraltar-source income, it must first register as an overseas company with the Gibraltar Companies Registry under Part 9 of the Companies Act 2014. Within 30 days of that registration, the entity must apply to the Income Tax Office on the prescribed non-resident company application form, attaching certified copies of the Cayman Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing, the registered office address, local contact details, and a declaration of the nature of Gibraltar activities. A Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) is issued within 15 working days. If the entity merely conducts cross-border online sales through Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal without a permanent establishment, no TIN is required and no Gibraltar income tax return is due.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections include: (a) group relief election under the Income Tax Act allowing surrender of trading losses within a 75% group; (b) an application for an advance tax ruling confirming non-resident status and territorial scope; (c) a procedural election under the Income Tax (Hybrid and Other Mismatches) Rules 2019 for alignment of accounting periods; and (d) participation exemption election on qualifying shareholdings. No election is available to treat the Cayman Exempted Company as a pass-through or transparent entity; it remains an entity-level taxable foreign company only to the extent it has Gibraltar-source profits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar has no VAT or GST (outside the EU VAT area); indirect taxation consists of import and excise duties on goods entering Gibraltar, while exports and offshore sales are not subject to any local consumption tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GIP 0.00 (no VAT registration threshold because no VAT law exists; any business undertaking import or export transactions must register with HM Customs of Gibraltar regardless of turnover).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate. Invoices must be retained under Gibraltar record-keeping rules. Customs declarations must be filed electronically through the Gibraltar Electronic Customs Declaration System (ECDS) using a Single Administrative Document (SAD); an electronic declaration reference is generated for each shipment. No government pre-approval of invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods manufactured in Gibraltar or re-exported from Gibraltar are outside the indirect tax base, creating an effective 0% rate by statutory design. To qualify, the goods must physically leave Gibraltar for a foreign destination, title must pass to the overseas customer, and the exporter must hold evidence of departure. There is no separate VAT refund mechanism because no input VAT exists; the zero-rating is achieved through non-taxability of the export transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ECDS declaration containing goods description, HS code 9504.90, net mass and export value)
Bill of Lading (or air waybill) evidencing despatch from Gibraltar port or airport to the foreign customer
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank FX confirmation showing receipt of export proceeds equal to the invoiced amount, with supporting payment ledger entries)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export transactions are scrutinised jointly by HM Customs of Gibraltar and the Income Tax Office. If the export zero-rating is claimed falsely or documentation is found to be fraudulent, the transaction is recharacterised as a local supply. The Commissioner may raise a Gibraltar income tax assessment on the full profit at 12.5% (or the applicable corporate rate), add interest at 8% per annum, and impose penalties up to 150% of the additional tax. Customs offences attract forfeiture of goods, fines up to £10,000, and imprisonment for up to 7 years. Any previously granted exemption or relief is subject to retrospective clawback for a period of up to six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), acting as the integrated banking and financial-services regulator under the Financial Services (Banking) Act; Gibraltar has no separate central bank, with sterling monetary authority residing in the Bank of England and HM Treasury, and note issuance for the Gibraltar pound undertaken by the Government of Gibraltar under statutory fiat.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital account and current account convertibility are fully unrestricted in Gibraltar and in the Cayman Islands. The Gibraltar pound is pegged at parity to GBP, and both GIP and GBP are freely convertible within the jurisdiction. For a Cayman Exempted Company operating through Gibraltar, profit remittance is not subject to withholding taxes or exchange-control approval. Dividends, royalties, loan repayments, and liquidation distributions may flow without deduction or prior authorisation. The only practical hurdles are anti-money-laundering documentary requirements, tax-residency determination, and any economic substance reporting obligations in the Cayman Islands.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or conversion ratio applies in Gibraltar or the Cayman Islands. A Cayman Exempted Company is free to retain export receipts in any convertible currency, with no mandatory timeline for repatriation and no obligation to convert into GIP, GBP, or KYD. The effective mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; all proceeds hold immediately and indefinitely at the Company's disposition.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Medium. Gibraltar- and UK-licensed electronic money institutions (e.g. Wise Business, Revolut Business, or specialised B2B FX platforms) generally decline Cayman Exempted Companies because of the non-resident tax-exempt status, opacity of the corporate register, and perceived Shell-company risk. Legal constraints under Gibraltar's Financial Services Act and UK e-money regulations prevent an unlicensed Cayman entity from holding e-money directly; it must be onboarded as a customer of a licensed EMI. Where an EMI does accept the structure, transaction limits are frequently capped and enhanced KYC is imposed. For Kickstarter/Stripe recurring collections, a dedicated merchant acquiring solution via a licensed PSP is materially more reliable than a general-purpose EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar banks permit remote onboarding for a Cayman Exempted Company where the beneficial ownership is transparent and the application is introduced by a regulated professional firm (e.g. a Gibraltar fiduciary or licensed accountant). Directors are not universally required to appear physically; however, a mandatory video conference and identity verification step applies. If the bank's compliance team flags elevated risk, or the Company's registers are not available through open public sources, a physical attendance at the Gibraltar branch may be demanded before final account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Exempted Company registered abroad but presenting for banking in Gibraltar, thus raising substance and commercial-nexus concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of directors and members; beneficial-ownership declaration aligned with Cayman BORSS requirements; notarised certificate of good standing; certificate of incumbency issued by the registered agent; audited or management accounts; a written substance plan demonstrating the Gibraltar link, including contracted office space, local director or fiduciary, and anticipated banking flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The underlying business is classified as 'handmade tabletop dice' but may appear inconsistent with the size of treasury flows if crowdfunding receipts are pooled through Kickstarter and Stripe.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial and revenue plan; Kickstarter campaign performance and payout reports; Stripe settlement statements; inventory photos with epoxy resin/pigment sourcing invoices; purchase agreements with fulfilment centres; and a clear reconciliation trail from payment gateway to the Company's Gibraltar bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-risk AML tier and online retail profile may still be rejected if there is a perceived overlap with gambling or gaming settlement rails due to Gibraltar's financial-centre association.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the ISIC 3240 registration and NAICS 339930 classification; product catalogue of polyhedral resin dice; customer invoices and sales terms; a clean pharmaceutical-and-gambling negative declaration; and a certified statement from the compliance officer that no prohibited sector is funded or serviced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity caused by shareholder loans and non-resident investors injecting initial capital from multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder loan agreements, board resolutions authorising capital injection, bank statements of the ultimate remitting accounts, notarised passports/corporate documents of the investors, and signed statutory declarations for the provenance of funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant shareholder capital injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT100 for legacy correspondent networks) using a clearly articulated beneficiary reference. The purpose code should read 'EQUI' (Equity Capital) or 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' in field 72, together with the Company's registration number and commercial invoice/board-minute reference. For same-day GBP sterling settlement into a Gibraltar bank, use CHAPS/Faster Payments for the final UK leg after converting USD/EUR via the receiving bank's FX desk. Verification obligations include a copy of the board resolution approving the capital call, a certificate of incumbency, source-of-funds statement, and the creditors' ledger entry on the Cayman share register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for pre-payments and invoice settlements to epoxy resin, pigment, and packaging suppliers. For larger bulk purchases, use a Sight Commercial Letter of Credit under ICC UCP600 with an MT700 issuance, with MT710/MT720 amendments as needed. Automatic clearing rails for small recurring disbursements include SEPA Credit Transfers in EUR within the EEA, UK Faster Payments in GBP, and Wise Business or Stripe Treasury for cross-border supplier payouts. Where the counterparty requires bank-to-bank reimbursement, use MT202 COV for underlying trade settlement after invoice verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contracts (deliverable) in GB, EUR, USD, and CHF
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to deliverability restrictions
Currency swaps for balancing dual-currency receivable streams
Over-the-counter European-style FX options (vanilla calls/puts) for risk-defined hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Islands Economic Substance Notification (ESN) - Non-Relevant Activity Attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority / Department for International Tax Co-operation (DITC e-filing portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January each year, filed concurrently with the Annual Return; companies incorporated in the second half of the year receive a deferral to the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic penalty of KYD 10,000 (USD 12,220) where the ESN remains outstanding beyond 60 days; continued default attracts further daily penalties up to KYD 50,000 and potential prosecution of directors and officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Islands Annual Return and Annual Government Fee (Exempted Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies / General Registry (CIMA Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January each year for all exempted companies in existence on the preceding 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts an automatic 33.33% surcharge if settled after 31 January and a 50% surcharge if settled after 15 April; protracted default leads to administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register (BORR) Annual Confirmation and Attestation of UBO Data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cayman Islands Corporate Registry (BORR Verification Portal) submitted through the licensed registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Change-driven updates within 15 days of any beneficial ownership event; annual confirmation of accuracy is filed together with the 31 January Annual Return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an accurate BORR attracts KYD 50,000 per company plus KYD 10,000 per day during continuing default; false attestation exposes officers to criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar External Company Annual Return (including UBO Confirmation Statement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (Registrar of Companies, Registry of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days of each anniversary of the date of registration of the external company in Gibraltar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts escalating penalties from GIP 150 to GIP 1,500 plus daily default fines; failure to file for 12 months or more risks administrative strike-off and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Income Tax Return (GRA) and Underlying Annual Financial Statements (12.5% corporate rate on Gibraltar-source profits)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 9 months after the end of the accounting period; where the GRA issues a filing notice, the return is due within 30 days of that notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial late-filing penalty of GIP 100 escalating to GIP 1,000; GRA may raise best-of-judgment assessments with interest at 3% over the base rate on unpaid tax; deliberate default carries criminal penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Cayman: no statutory audit is required for this unregulated exempted company unless it is licensed under the Banks and Trust Companies Act, Insurance Act, Securities Investment Business Act, or Mutual Funds Act. Gibraltar: a mandatory audit applies only to a 'large company' (turnover exceeding GIP 10.2M, gross assets exceeding GIP 5.1M, or more than 50 employees) or where members holding at least 10% serve an audit notice; this artisanal e-commerce dice manufacturer qualifies for the small-company audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Cayman: no statutory accounts filing obligation exists; IFRS is the accepted practice for any prepared general-purpose accounts. Gibraltar: IFRS or Gibraltar-adopted UK GAAP (FRS 102; Section 1A for micro-entities) is acceptable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Cayman BORR: the licensed registered office files UBO particulars on the CIMA verification portal at incorporation and within 15 days of any share-transfer-driven change in control; an annual attestation of accuracy accompanies the January Annual Return. Gibraltar: the external company's annual return operates as the confirmation statement, attesting continuing beneficial-owner data; any share transfer altering beneficial control must be consistent with the Gibraltar Registry of Companies records at each annual filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 2,000 - 3,500 per year (Cayman CSP/registered office plus Gibraltar registered-office compliance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,500 - 12,000 for a voluntary audit; no mandatory audit applies to this micro-sized unregulated e-commerce company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 10% (flat Gibraltar corporate income tax rate on chargeable profits under the Income Tax Act 2010, s.10)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday remains; the pre-2011 Gibraltar exempt-company regime was abolished in line with EU state-aid decisions. The effective rate for a Cayman Exempted Company is 0% if central management and control and all trading activity remain outside Gibraltar, because Gibraltar employs a territorial/source-based taxation system. For Gibraltar-source profits, the effective rate is reduced below 10% by 100% first-year capital allowances on qualifying plant and machinery used in dice casting, R&D-style design expenditure deductions, and loss relief carried forward (indefinite by statute; conservative 5-year recognition applied in compliance modelling). No VAT, no capital gains tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 120 (Gibraltar Company Income Tax Return); e-filed through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office online filing portal (Self-Assessment e-Services)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deliverable within 30 days of the Commissioner's Notice to File; for accounting periods ending on 30 June in the preceding Gibraltar year of assessment (1 July to 30 June), the compliance deadline is capped at 9 months after the accounting period end; non-resident companies with a Gibraltar permanent establishment must file on the same timetable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: Gibraltar Companies Registry number, legal form (Cayman Exempted Company), registered office and local agent in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Gibraltar branch/PE registration number and the name of the locally appointed agent; do not omit the Cayman registration and ELF ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period covered by the return (basis period).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the 12-month period ending within the Gibraltar year of assessment; a Cayman Exempted Company may use its Cayman fiscal year-end if no Gibraltar PE books are maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residence status: resident / non-resident with PE / non-resident without PE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'non-resident with PE' only if the company has a fixed place of business in Gibraltar (workshop, warehouse, employees). A purely Cayman-administered seller of dice is not resident and files a nil return or no return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gibraltar-source trading profits: gross proceeds from tabletop dice and accessories attributable to the Gibraltar PE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Kickstarter, Stripe and PayPal receipts net of refunds attributable to the Gibraltar establishment; exclude sales booked and administered entirely by the Cayman entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded from the Gibraltar charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign-source income (e.g., UK/EU crowdfunding sales managed offshore) in the memorandum column; such income is not taxable in Gibraltar but is disclosed for CRS/FATCA and economic substance purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: costs of raw materials (epoxy resin, moulds), platform fees, payment processing charges, packaging and shipping, wages and premises costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deductions incurred by and for the Gibraltar PE are allowable; head-office costs of the Cayman entity are not deductible unless recharged on an arm's length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances claimed on qualifying plant, machinery and industrial fixtures used in dice casting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim 100% first-year allowance on qualifying production equipment held in Gibraltar; no depreciation per se is allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted chargeable profit or loss for the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute as Box 4 minus Box 6 and Box 7; non-residents must maintain contemporaneous local accounts reconciling the PE result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss relief brought forward and terminal loss relief claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the lower of available losses and current profits; statute provides indefinite carry-forward but the audited model recognises a five-year horizon for the Cayman/Gibraltar structure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable: 10% of chargeable profits after loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with PE must pay via direct debit from a Gibraltar EMI/bank account; no instalment regime applies below the de minimis threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration: director or authorised tax agent signature and date, together with the tax agent's licence number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A director of the Cayman Exempted Company must sign under declaration of truthfulness; knowingly false declarations expose the director to personal liability under the Income Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: fixed penalty of GIP 300; continuing daily penalty up to GIP 100 per day; the Commissioner may issue an estimated assessment with interest from the due date; fraudulent or negligent returns incur a tax-geared penalty up to 100% of the tax under-assessed, plus summary or indictable criminal fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Gibraltar does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid by a Gibraltar company or Gibraltar branch to its shareholders, including non-resident shareholders of a Cayman Exempted Company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is necessary for Gibraltar-origin dividends because domestic WHT is nil. Where treaty relief is sought against foreign-source payments (e.g., UK royalties under the UK-Gibraltar double taxation arrangement), the Cayman/Gibraltar chain must: (i) obtain a Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) supported by a valid ESR file and Cayman tax-exemption confirmation; (ii) submit the completed DTA claim form to the UK HMRC or the payer together with the current TRC; (iii) evidence beneficial ownership of the underlying IP or shareholding; (iv) include the payment in the CRS/FATCA filings. Cayman imposes no WHT on such payments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 0% withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest paid by Gibraltar to non-residents. The UK-Gibraltar DTA and EU interest/royalty protections do not impose source taxes on Gibraltar; for the reverse flow (Gibraltar payer to Cayman licensor/lender), no Gibraltar WHT or Cayman tax arises, but the payer must obtain a valid withholding-tax exemption certificate only where the transaction is routed through a treaty jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP 500,000 aggregate value of related-party transactions in an accounting period requires a full Gibraltar Local File; a GIP 5,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers a Master File; below these thresholds the company must still retain a one-page TP policy, functional analysis and benchmarking memorandum based on OECD principles.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (open-market comparables for polyhedral dice and resin components)
Resale Price Method (crowdfunding and retail distribution via Kickstarter/Stripe)
Cost Plus Method (custom epoxy casting and finishing services)
TNMM (net margin of the Gibraltar PE against PayPal/Stripe-channel comparables)
Profit Split (allocation of brand intangibles and manufacturing IP between Cayman parent and Gibraltar trading entity)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar applies the OECD/EU Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for geographically mobile activities, including distribution and IP exploitation. The Cayman Exempted Company using Gibraltar as a booking or payment gateway must demonstrate: physical office or workshop in Gibraltar; minimum of one director and one employee physically present (where applicable); board meetings in Gibraltar with substantive minutes; core income-generating activities (dice design, mould maintenance, order fulfilment decisions, payment risk management) performed in Gibraltar; and adequate operating expenditure. Non-compliance triggers denial of tax residence certificate, reassessment of profits and administrative penalties, plus possible strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Kickstarter, Stripe or PayPal revenue while claiming a zero-tax Cayman exemption, even though a fixed Gibraltar workshop or employees create a taxable permanent establishment; procuring a false Form 120 Box 11 declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On summary conviction: fine up to GIP 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months; on indictment: unlimited fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; the Commissioner may raise escaped assessments for up to 6 prior years with interest and a penalty of 100% of the tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or knowingly cause a false return are personally and severally liable for the assessed tax shortfall, face criminal conviction, disqualification from acting as a director for up to 15 years, and the court may impose a departure prohibition order preventing them from leaving Gibraltar until the tax and penalties are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the Cayman Exempted Company as a 'pure mailbox' with no office, employees or board meetings in Gibraltar, while directing all daily operations through foreign subcontractors and booking profits offshore to exploit the tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the corporate form; reassessment of all Gibraltar-source profits at 10%; ESR administrative fine of GIP 5,000 to GIP 20,000 per failure; cancellation of the Gibraltar tax residence certificate and Companies Registry strike-off; referral to the Criminal Investigation Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the reassessed taxes and ESR penalties, face disqualification orders under the Companies Act 2014, seizure of personal assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, and travel bans while the tax debt is under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CTF Failure in Payment Rail Operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating multiple Stripe, PayPal and Kickstarter accounts without corporate KYC/CDD, commingling campaign proceeds with personal accounts, failing to file suspicious activity reports (SARs) with the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit, or having no documented source of funds for large prepaid dice pre-orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and the Gibraltar AML/CFT Code: unlimited fines on conviction for money laundering (up to 14 years imprisonment); regulatory penalties of up to GIP 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; account freezes and forfeiture orders; mandatory revocation of EMI and payment-processing arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to confiscation orders over personal wealth derived from the offending, disqualification, imprisonment for up to 14 years for money laundering, and cross-border travel bans pending extradition or mutual legal assistance requests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive royalties or management fees from the Gibraltar trading operation to the Cayman parent, or selling dice moulds and brand IP to the Cayman entity at non-arm's length prices to strip Gibraltar taxable profits below the exemption threshold; absence of contemporaneous TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Commissioner's TP adjustment restoring the arm's length profit with interest; disallowance of the royalty/fee deduction; penalty of 100% of the under-declared tax; joint audit by the Gibraltar Commissioner and HMRC under the UK-Gibraltar exchange of information arrangement; publication of the adjustment as a serious-compliance breach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute artificial TP policies are jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties, may be prohibited from holding any Gibraltar corporate appointment, and face criminal prosecution for cheating the public revenue with imprisonment up to 5 years.
